key_insight: LLM-driven performance optimization rarely reduced execution energy relative to human reference code, while adding substantial inference energy costs.
engineering_relevance: Measure optimization and execution energy together, and prioritize model architecture and output-token limits rather than assuming faster code is greener.
method: Evaluate 11 open-source LLMs under four decoding configurations on all 1,000 EffiBench problems.
Collect per-process, hardware-level energy measurements during iterative code optimization and execution.
Compare generated code with canonical human references and estimate energy break-even points.
evidence_signal: Of 44 configurations, 42 produced code using 4%–886% more execution energy than human references; the two energy-saving configurations required roughly 10^6–10^7 executions to offset optimization costs.
watch_item: Results are specific to the evaluated benchmark, models, and measurement setup; assess energy savings on deployment workloads before adopting self-refinement.
paper_title: Green Code or Costly Code? Evaluating the Energy Costs of Iterative LLM-Based Code Optimizations
